setup.why: report id and project id were provided directly by the probe assignment (report 10393 / identifier SC-492, our own report created by an earlier campaign in project 379335744 / PR-2005), not obtained via the id-pool fixture or invoked here

notes:
READ vs WRITE: describeCapability declares mode:"write" despite the name/intent being read-shaped ("download"). Confirmed correct on the evidence: the call does not fetch or return existing bytes — it kicks off a new async export job in a background worker each time it is invoked (a side-effecting action with its own job/channel, not an idempotent retrieval), so 'write' is the right classification even though a caller experiences it as 'downloading a report'. Invoked with user_permission granted and a change_summary per the write protocol.

Invoke succeeded first attempt, zero drift: declared response {channel, success} matched the actual body exactly -> {"channel":"996cbba6-3e8d-4417-bdb7-dc8919d52998","success":true}. No file bytes, base64 blob, or redirect came back at any point -- so the 'if it returns binary' question does not arise here, unlike import_dataset_c_s_v's multipart-send gap this is not a JSON-transport casualty, it never attempts to carry the file at all.

STRUCTURAL FINDING -- this is a THIRD confirmed instance of the 'mints a handle nothing can redeem' pattern already found twice in this campaign (get_report_attachment_url: structurally unreachable, no capability produces its attachment_id; export_dashboard_analytics: export_id is a correlation token only, generic status/download endpoints report pending forever / 404). download_report's own contract is honest about this in its guidance text ('no endpoint to poll it and no way to fetch the artefact through the API'), so this is not a contract-accuracy defect in this one capability -- the declared behaviour and the live behaviour agree exactly. It is a coverage gap in the profile as a whole: the input side works (project_id + report_id resolve fine against our real report 10393/SC-492), but the output side mints a websocket-pushed 'channel' uuid that no other capability in the tm profile can subscribe to, poll, or redeem. This capability is already listed (previously undocumented as untested) in tests/live/findings/unobservable-jobs-systemic.md, which has been updated with this run's concrete confirmation.

PREREQUISITE vs DEFECT: report 10393/SC-492 is deliberately unscheduled (frequency:null, no mail_to) so it plausibly has never been generated as an output before. That is irrelevant to this call's own semantics, though -- download_report always starts a fresh export job on every invocation; it does not read a previously-produced artifact, so there is no 'nothing to download yet' precondition to distinguish from a bug. Verdict is UNVERIFIED rather than PASS/DRIFT for the same reason as the sibling capabilities in the systemic finding: the suite judges writes on whether the effect (a usable file) actually landed, and that is unobservable by construction here -- 'the request was accepted' is the most that can honestly be claimed.

NO EMAIL TRIGGERED: file_type=csv only initiates a background export pushed over a realtime channel; the contract exposes no recipient list, send flag, or scheduling field for this capability (those live on the held-back send_report_email_now_v1 sibling, not here), and report 10393 remains unscheduled/no mail_to throughout. Nothing in this probe could have mailed anything.

create_report/update_report shared-serializer check: out of scope for this probe (download_report's own response has no mail_to, project_ids, or included_projects fields to compare -- its declared and actual shape is just {channel, success}), so no evidence either way was produced here on that separate finding.
